items.text: Conclusion so far: $M$ is of finite type and flat (if $k$ is noetherian this means projective of finite type). Without noetherian hypothesis: show $M$ of finite presentation.
0\to R\to L\to M\to 0,\qquad L\ \text{free of finite type};\quad M\ \text{finitely presented}\iff R\ \text{of finite type}
$M$ flat, so the sequence stays exact after $\otimes k^I$; also after $(\ )^I$:
\begin{array}{ccccccccc}0&\to&R\otimes k^I&\to&L\otimes k^I&\to&M\otimes k^I&\to&0\\&&\downarrow&&\downarrow&&\downarrow&&\\0&\to&R^I&\to&L^I&\to&M^I&\to&0\end{array}
Vertical arrows isomorphisms for $L$ (free of finite type) and $M$, hence for $R$: so $R$ is of finite type.
$W(M)$ representable $\Rightarrow$ $M$ flat of finite presentation $\Rightarrow$ $M$ projective of finite type.
The functor $V(M)$
V(M)\colon k'\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-mod}}(M,k')\qquad(\text{a module over }\mathcal O)
Claim. $V(M)$ is representable for every $M$.
V(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}\bigl(S_k(M),\,-\bigr),\qquad S_k(M)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}S^n_k(M)
$M$ free of rank $n$: $S_k(M)$ = polynomial algebra in $n$ indeterminates.
$V(M)$ of finite type (resp. finite presentation) over $k$ iff $M$ is of finite type (resp. finite presentation).
$M\mapsto W(M)$ covariant, $M\mapsto V(M)$ contravariant, into module functors over $\mathcal O$.
$M$ is not recovered from the group functor alone (in characteristic $p$, additive endomorphisms of $\mathbb G_a$ need not be linear); one must use the $\mathcal O$-module structure.
Both functors are fully faithful: for $k$-modules $M,N$

\operatorname{Hom}_k(M,N)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}\bigl(W(M),W(N)\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{Hom}_k(M,N)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}\bigl(V(N),V(M)\bigr)
Proof: take $k$-valued points to get the inverse map; check both composites are the identity.
Duality between $W(M)$ and $V(M)$
V(M)\times W(M)\longrightarrow\mathcal O,\qquad \operatorname{Hom}(M,k')\times (M\otimes k')\to k'

W(M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal O}\bigl(V(M),\mathcal O\bigr),\qquad V(M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal O}\bigl(W(M),\mathcal O\bigr)
Biduality theorem: each of $W(M)$, $V(M)$ is the dual of the other, hence reflexive — for all $M$, whereas $M\simeq M^{\vee\vee}$ needs $M$ projective of finite type.
$M$ projective of finite type, $N=M^\vee$:
W(M)\simeq V(N),\qquad W(M)(k')=M\otimes k'=\operatorname{Hom}_k(N,k')
W(M)\ \text{is represented by}\ S_k(M^\vee)
